title: See what the road height changes from the driver’s seat
summary: A July 2022 KartaView drive records a north-facing view along I Street in Anchorage. Both native Metal frames use its reported GPS and heading and the same nine map tiles. The horizontal field of view is estimated at 78°. The former terrain lifts the pavement and building on the right into a bank. The revised terrain gives the street a substantially flatter cross-section.
measurement: A separate test around the corner used the actual Miata physics on K Street. The old car rolled backward at the approach. The new car cleared 47 m and made four-wheel contact in all 708 driving ticks. Across 154 occupied 5 m cells on surveyed Anchorage roads, median ground-relief error fell from 2.52 m to 0.81 m. The street photo also shows parked cars, lane position, building materials and overcast light that the game still misses.

images.caption: I Street looking north. Photograph, same scene with the previous ground, and USGS ground. Repeated previous-ground controls differed by 0.044 RGB levels per channel on average (0–255).
